title: Prescribed differential fibre bases give principal etale polynomial charts
statement: Let R and A be commutative rings, with A a smooth R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and let K be a field [def-weil-field] with an A-algebra structure. Let I be a finite set, h:I to A a family, b an A-basis of the Kahler module Omega_{A/R} [def-weil-pbc-free-module, def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and c a K-basis of K tensor_A Omega_{A/R} [def-weil-module-base-change] indexed by the same I. Suppose c_i=1 tensor dh_i for every i. Then there is f in A with nonzero image in K such that the polynomial evaluation map R[T_i:i in I] to A[1/f], T_i maps to h_i/1 [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-ring-localization-away], is etale. Here etale means finitely presented and formally etale: its Kahler module and first cotangent homology vanish. Empty I is allowed.

source.place: Tag 02GU (lemma-etale-at-point), differential criterion; algebra.tex Tag 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth), part (2). Agent-written determinant-of-differential-basis variant, using the proved source-library polynomial-evaluation criterion.

proof.text: Set v_i=dh_i and let M be the matrix of v in the basis b. Set f=det M [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. The base-changed basis b_K has coefficient matrix obtained by applying A to K entrywise. Since v becomes the basis c, this coefficient matrix is invertible. Determinants commute with ring homomorphisms; hence the image of f in K is nonzero. Formally, Module.Basis.isUnit_det and RingHom.map_det give this directly.

Put S=A[1/f] [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. In the base-changed basis b_S, the vectors 1 tensor v_i have coefficient matrix M_S with unit determinant f/1. The adjugate gives an inverse to M_S, so the vectors are an S-basis, including when I is empty. This is Module.Basis.is_basis_iff_det.

Localization A to S is formally etale. The canonical differential equivalence [lem-trf-formally-etale-differentials-base-change] takes 1 tensor dh_i to d(h_i/1). Thus these latter vectors form an S-basis of Omega_{S/R}. Smoothness and finite presentation over R persist under principal localization. Apply the already-proved source-library theorem MvPolynomial.etale_aeval_of_basis_kaehlerDifferential (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.RingTheory.Etale.Kaehler). Its proof uses the polynomial differential basis to identify S tensor_{R[T]} Omega_{R[T]/R} to Omega_{S/R} with a basis isomorphism. The Jacobi-Zariski exact sequence and H1(L_{S/R})=0 give H1(L_{S/R[T]})=0, and the differential transitivity sequence gives Omega_{S/R[T]}=0. Finite presentation over R implies finite presentation over R[T]. Hence the specified evaluation map is etale.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_etale_aeval_localization_of_fibre_basis
    {R A K ι : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Field K]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra A K] [Algebra.Smooth R A] [Finite ι]
    (h : ι → A) (b : Module.Basis ι A (KaehlerDifferential R A))
    (c : Module.Basis ι K (K ⊗[A] KaehlerDifferential R A))
    (hc : ∀ i, c i = 1 ⊗ₜ[A] KaehlerDifferential.D R A (h i)) :
    ∃ f : A, algebraMap A K f ≠ 0 ∧
      (aeval (fun i => algebraMap A (Localization.Away f) (h i)) :
        MvPolynomial ι R →ₐ[R] Localization.Away f).toRingHom.Etale
